newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand raps Malaysia papers for AIDS cartoons.
newsitem.headline: Thailand raps Malaysia papers for AIDS cartoons.

text.p: Thailand on Wednesday complained about two cartoons which appeared in Malaysian newspapers, saying the images did not create a conducive atmosphere for a meeting of ASEAN nations later this week.

A senior foreign ministry official said in a statement that Thailand and its people were "saddened and disappointed" after the cartoons were published in the New Sunday Times and its daily the New Straits Times this week.
The cartoons connected Singaporean tourists to concerns about AIDS in Thailand.
Malaysian Foreign Minister Abdullah Badawi said he had yet to receive a complaint, but advised Malaysian newspapers to be careful with how they portrayed other countries.
"The level of sensitivities differed... Some will not care less but others will take exception to it," Abdullah was quoted as saying by Malaysia's national Bernama news agency.

Thai foreign ministry spokesman Surapong Jayanama said the controversial cartoons were motivated by the current squabbling between Malaysia and Singapore, and accused the Malaysian press of trying to drag Thailand into the conflict.

"This makes the Thai government and its people saddened and disappointed," he said. "Such an act has given a negative impact to the good image of the country and any friendly countries should not have done this to each other."

Ties between Singapore and Malaysia took a dive earlier this year after Singapore's Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew made disparaging remarks about the southern Malaysian state of Johor, saying it was "notorious for shootings, muggings and car-jacking".

One cartoon depicted a group of Singaporeans queueing at an immigration checkpoint waiting to tour Thailand and Indonesia, while a man resembling Lee distributed condoms, reminding them to use the contraceptives when on holiday in the two countries.
The other depicted Singaporean tourists going through an AIDS checkpoint on their return home from Thailand.
The New Straits Times Press (Malaysia) Bhd, which publishes the two newspapers, has not reacted to the complaint.
Abdullah said the matter would most likely be discussed at an ASEAN Foreign Ministers' meeting in Kuala Lumpur on Saturday.
"Whenever there's something, we use the meeting to discuss matters arising," Abdullah said.
ASEAN -- grouping Indonesia, Malaysia, Brunei, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam -- will discuss when to admit Burma, Laos and Cambodia as members.
Surapong said the incident created a sour note ahead of Saturday's meeting.

"It goes against normal practices of friendly countries and especially in this case did not create a conducive atmosphere for welcoming foreign ministers from friendly countries, like Thailand, which is due to attend the May 31 meeting in Kuala Lumpur," he said.
ASEAN countries, which have widely different religious and cultural traditions, have a policy of trying not to criticise one another.
Thailand, which has a thriving sex industry, has been praised by U.N. officials for boosting condom usage to prevent the spread of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome.
